rows.notes: [2026-08-25] MOVED+REWORDED -- flag for review: relocated from docs/specification/checkout-rest.md (old, standalone sentence outside any named subsection) to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md, now under a new '#### Update Buyer Info' subsection. NEW (2026-08-25) quote: "Outside `complete_in_progress`, each Update Checkout replaces the entire Checkout session, so the Platform **MUST** include all previously set fields it intends to retain." Substance is the same full-replacement/retain-fields obligation, but the new text (a) adds an explicit carve-out scoping the rule to outside complete_in_progress (a new state-dependent condition tied to the new Actions/complete_in_progress-freeze model), and (b) promotes the obligation to an explicit bold MUST on 'the Platform' rather than lowercase 'clients must'. rows.requirement: Complete Checkout response is the checkout object; when completion finishes synchronously status is completed and order is populated with id and permalink_url, when accepted for async processing status is complete_in_progress and order is absent
rows.quote:
The response is the checkout object: ... When completion finishes synchronously, `status` is `completed` and the
    `order` field is present, providing necessary identifiers such as `id` and
    `permalink_url` that can be used to reference the full state of the placed
    order.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] MOVED+REWORDED -- flag for review: relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md), Complete Checkout section. OLD (2026-04-08) quote: "The response of this call is the checkout object with the `order` field populated in it. The returned `order` provides necessary identifiers, such as `id` and `permalink_url`, that can be used to reference the full state of the placed order." NEW (2026-08-25) quote: "The response is the checkout object: * When completion finishes synchronously, `status` is `completed` and the `order` field is present, providing necessary identifiers such as `id` and `permalink_url` that can be used to reference the full state of the placed order. * When completion is accepted for asynchronous processing, `status` is `complete_in_progress` and no `order` is present. ... * Any other status retains its core Checkout status lifecycle semantics." This is a materially restructured, conditional rewrite: the old text unconditionally said the response has order populated; the new text splits into three branches (sync-completed-with-order, async-complete_in_progress-without-order, any-other-status) tied to the new complete_in_progress/Actions machinery introduced in this release. The row's own quote above is the true verbatim new sync-completion branch (still the branch the old oracle exercises). Descriptive 'is' normalized to MUST. Oracle: test_complete_checkout asserts order, order.id, order.permalink_url present -- this remains valid for the synchronous-completion branch the suite exercises, but does NOT cover the new async complete_in_progress branch (no order) -- candidate for a new oracle row/probe.

rows.requirement: All requests MUST include the UCP-Agent header containing the platform profile URI (RFC 8941 dictionary syntax)
rows.quote:
**UCP-Agent**: All requests **MUST** include the `UCP-Agent` header
    containing the platform profile URI using Dictionary Structured Field syntax
    ([RFC 8941](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8941){target="_blank"}).

rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md (was checkout-rest.md); wording unchanged. Request-side header requirement on the platform; checked on requests, not on the checkout response body. Reclassified 2026-07-03 (adversarial review F2, suite-wide policy): 'All requests MUST include the UCP-Agent header' binds the REQUEST AUTHOR (platform) -- the spec mandates no business-side rejection of header-less requests, so a merchant check grading a 4xx is a contrapositive stretch that can false-deviate a tolerant conformant merchant (same subject-binding as ORD-015/DISC-006, decided the same way for consistency). The suite's own probe traffic satisfies the MUST. Candidate for a client-bound exemption once version-scoped exemptions land.

rows.requirement: When an Idempotency-Key is provided, server MUST store the key+result >=24h, return the cached result for a duplicate key whose request body matches the original, and return 409 if the key is reused with a mismatched body
rows.quote:
When provided, the server **MUST**:
    1. Store the key with the operation result for at least 24 hours.
    2. Return the cached result for duplicate keys whose request body matches the original.
    3. Return `409 Conflict` if the key is reused with a mismatched body.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] MOVED+REWORDED -- flag for review: relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md (was checkout-rest.md), still under Idempotency-Key. OLD (2026-04-08) quote: "When provided, the server MUST: 1. Store the key with the operation result for at least 24 hours. 2. Return the cached result for duplicate keys. 3. Return 409 Conflict if the key is reused with different parameters." NEW (2026-08-25) quote: "When provided, the server MUST: 1. Store the key with the operation result for at least 24 hours. 2. Return the cached result for duplicate keys whose request body matches the original. 3. Return 409 Conflict if the key is reused with a mismatched body." Item 1 is byte-identical. Items 2 and 3 are materially clarified: 'duplicate keys' now explicitly means 'whose request body matches the original' (previously undefined what made a request a 'duplicate'), and '409 on different parameters' is now '409 on a mismatched body' -- same intent but now normatively ties the duplicate/conflict distinction to a body-match test. A new immediately-following sentence also cross-references '../../signatures.md#replay-protection' for the full payload-matching contract, which did not exist before. This could change how a conformance oracle judges 'duplicate' vs 'reused with different parameters', so flagged for human review. Covered by separate idempotency_test.py (not in scope read).

rows.quote:
**Protocol errors**: Return appropriate HTTP status code (401, 403, 409, 429,
    503) with JSON body containing `code` and `content`.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md (was checkout-rest.md); wording unchanged. Distinguishes protocol errors (HTTP status) from business outcomes (HTTP 200 + messages).

rows.requirement: Business outcomes (including unavailable merchandise) return HTTP 200 with the UCP envelope and messages array
rows.quote: **Business outcomes**: Return HTTP 200 with UCP envelope and `messages` array.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md (was checkout-rest.md); wording unchanged. Behavioral; needs a receiver that produces a business-outcome scenario.

rows.requirement: When no resource exists to act on, messages SHOULD use severity: unrecoverable
rows.quote:
When no resource exists to act on, messages SHOULD use
`severity: "unrecoverable"`.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged. Error-handling behavior; severity enum itself is in message schema (not base checkout.json).

rows.requirement: On create with all items unavailable, response carries ucp.status:error with messages and no resource body
rows.quote:
When the business cannot create a new resource or the requested resource
no longer exists, the response contains `ucp.status: "error"` with
`messages` describing the failure — no resource is included in the
response body.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged. Descriptive normative behavior; ucp.status is the shape discriminator. Restated in rest.md's Business Outcomes section.

rows.requirement: Businesses SHOULD surface requires_buyer_input/review messages as early as possible; platforms SHOULD prioritize resolving recoverable errors before initiating handoff
rows.quote:
Businesses **SHOULD** surface such messages as early as possible, and platforms
**SHOULD** prioritize resolving recoverable errors before initiating handoff.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged (a new following sentence about Actions/re-evaluation was added -- not part of this quote). Two SHOULDs (business + platform) about error-stack ordering.

rows.requirement: Platforms MUST NOT autonomously complete a checkout with mismatched totals; SHOULD reject or escalate for buyer review via continue_url
rows.quote:
However, platforms MUST NOT autonomously complete
a checkout with mismatched totals. Platforms SHOULD reject the checkout or
escalate and ask for buyer review via `continue_url`.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged. Constrains autonomous Complete (relevant to ready_for_complete autonomy). Platform-side; lower-case 'must not' in prose, normative.

rows.requirement: Businesses MUST NOT complete a transaction with unresolved eligibility claims; accepted claims MUST be resolved before completion
rows.quote:
Businesses **MUST NOT** complete a transaction with unresolved eligibility
claims.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged; also restated at L681-682 'but all accepted claims **MUST** be resolved before the transaction can complete.' Completion-gating invariant. Prose-only.

rows.requirement: Get Checkout honors the business-provided TTL via expires_at; after cancel/complete the business decides what to return
rows.quote:
After cancellation or
completion it is up to the business on what to return (i.e this can be a long
lived state or expire after a particular TTL - resulting in a 'not found'
error). From the platform there is no specific enforcement for a TTL of the
checkout.
rows.notes: [2026-08-25] relocated to docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md (was checkout.md); wording unchanged. Business discretion on post-terminal Get behavior; expires_at default TTL 6h (schema L120).

notes: Schema file is vendored at conformance/.vendor/ucp-2026-08-25/source/schemas/shopping/checkout.json and remains at the same relative path as 2026-04-08 (source/schemas/shopping/checkout.json); only line numbers shifted (a new 'actions' response field was inserted for the Actions/extension machinery introduced in this release).

Doc reorg: docs/specification/checkout.md -> docs/specification/shopping/checkout/index.md; docs/specification/checkout-rest.md -> docs/specification/shopping/checkout/rest.md. All in-doc cross-reference links updated accordingly (e.g. 'checkout.md#create-checkout' -> 'index.md#create-checkout'); this is a pure relocation, not a substance change, for every CARRIED row.

Confirmed $ref relocations into common/types/: within checkout.json, the 'signals' field's $ref moved from 'types/signals.json' to '../common/types/signals.json' (CHK-042, RENAMED) and the 'context' field's $ref moved from a shopping-local type to '../common/types/context.json' (noted under CHK-041, does not affect that row's quoted text). 'totals' also now $refs '../common/types/totals.json'. By contrast 'attribution' and 'order' kept their shopping-local $refs (types/attribution.json, types/order_confirmation.json) -- the relocation was selective, not blanket, so each $ref was verified individually rather than assumed.

The prompt's warning that an 'ucp_request' sub-object of {create,update,complete} was simplified to a single string value in at least one sibling schema does NOT apply to any field in checkout.json itself: line_items, buyer, context, and payment all retain the full {create,update,complete} sub-object form unchanged from 2026-04-08.

Three rows are flagged REWORDED for human review because the 08-25 prose materially changed scope or conditions rather than just relocating: CHK-024 (Update Checkout full-replacement duty gained an explicit 'outside complete_in_progress' carve-out), CHK-025 (Complete Checkout response shape was split into synchronous-completed-with-order vs asynchronous-complete_in_progress-without-order branches), and CHK-048 (Idempotency-Key duplicate/conflict semantics were clarified to hinge on request-body matching). One row is RENAMED: CHK-042 (signals' $ref path moved into common/types/).

No row in this area was found to be DEAD -- every 2026-04-08 checkout-lifecycle requirement has a located 2026-08-25 equivalent, confirmed by direct reading of shopping/checkout/index.md, shopping/checkout/rest.md, and source/schemas/shopping/checkout.json (all three read in full).

official_oracle=true rows are backed by conformance/.vendor/conformance/checkout_lifecycle_test.py (create/get/update/complete/cancel happy paths; terminal-state immutability via test_cannot_{update,cancel,complete}_{completed,canceled}_checkout; cancel idempotency; status-enum assertions). That suite is pinned to spec 2026-01-23 -- assertions are version-stable for these lifecycle invariants, but the version delta is noted, and CHK-025's new asynchronous complete_in_progress branch is NOT covered by the existing oracle (candidate for a new probe). Idempotency MUSTs (CHK-047/048) are likely covered by a separate idempotency_test.py that was out of scope and not inspected.

schema_enforced=true only for genuine JSON-Schema constructs on checkout.json: status enum (CHK-033) and response required[] (CHK-034). All 'ucp_request' annotations (omit/required/optional per operation) are UCP-specific, NOT standard JSON-Schema keywords -- a vanilla draft 2020-12 validator against base checkout.json would not enforce them, hence schema_enforced=false for CHK-035..043 (a UCP-aware request-profile validator would catch these).

continue_url MUST-be-absolute-HTTPS (CHK-004) is schema_enforced=false: the schema only declares format:'uri', which most validators treat as annotation-only and which permits http/relative; the absolute-HTTPS constraint is prose-only.

State-transition legality and terminal-state immutability (CHK-017) are prose invariants, not schema-encoded -- base checkout.json has no if/then or transition modeling. Their oracle is behavioral (HTTP non-200 on illegal transition).

Lifecycle terminal states remain completed and canceled; complete_in_progress, incomplete, requires_escalation, ready_for_complete are non-terminal. Autonomous Complete is permitted only from ready_for_complete (CHK-031). This release adds a substantial new 'Actions' extension-point concept layered onto the same six-state lifecycle (see index.md '### Actions' and '#### Accepted completion') -- no old row maps to it since it is wholly new normative material, not a reworded carry of anything in the 2026-04-08 register; it is out of scope for this extraction (which only carries forward the 57 existing 04-08 rows) but is flagged here for a possible future new-row addition.

Several requirements are platform-side behaviors (CHK-008/009/010/029/030/055) or out-of-band side effects (CHK-011 confirmation email) that cannot be validated from a single business HTTP response; marked manual or needs-receiver accordingly.

REST examples still include a 'deprecated' top-level id in some request bodies with a comment that id is provided in the URL path -- consistent with CHK-035 (id is ucp_request:omit on requests) but shows real-world payloads still send it.
